title: Opportunities and Challenges for Advanced Imaging, Spectroscopy and Radiomics in Paediatric Neuro-Oncology: Mapping Innovations to the Patient Journey for Children and Young People
content: Central nervous system tumours remain the leading cause of cancer death in children and young people and include a wide diversity of tumour types and behaviours. Advances in molecular technologies have revolutionised the diagnostic landscape of these tumours. In parallel to this, imaging technologies, digitisation and quantification of radiological images and radiomics, have continued to evolve, providing increasing insight beyond the anatomy of a tumour, interrogating tumour properties and providing novel biomarkers. Such information is critical in guiding treatment decisions and in the evaluation, approval and implementation of novel therapies and treatment strategies. In this review, we highlight and summarise recent advances in imaging technologies, radiomics, including the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI). We map the key developments, opportunities and challenges to the patient journey, including, non-invasive pre-surgery diagnosis, biological pathway assessment, risk stratification, treatment planning, response assessment and prediction and monitoring of long-term consequences of tumour and treatment. Challenges and potential solutions across data availability, analysis pipelines and implementation and validation within clinical practice are then summarised. We propose the next decade will see a paradigm shift in analysis of radiological images, combining traditional qualitative radiological assessment, with advanced and quantitative and AI approaches, similar to the transformation of pathology, from a histological to a combined molecular-pathological classification.
